pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

9. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water always increases oxygen

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.

11. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. newton (N)
   D. pascal (Pa)

12. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

1. D — Ice melting to water

2. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

4. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.

5. D — 100 °C

6. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.

7. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.

8. B — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. A — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

10. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.

11. C — newton (N)

12. B — Glucose and oxygen

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reproduction in plants; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of The Interdependence of Life; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
